name: Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Kaysān
summary: Baghdad grammarian who studied with both al-Mubarrad and Thaʿlab and joined what he learnt from the two schools.
bio: Ibn Kaysān learnt Basran grammar from al-Mubarrad and Kufan from Thaʿlab, and the sources describe him as knowing both and keeping to neither: one of the first of the grammarians later called 'Baghdadi'. Al-Zubaydī places him among Thaʿlab's companions, in the sixth Kufan generation. His books on the grammar of the Qurʾān, on the masculine and feminine and a short grammar, al-Muwaffaqī, are known by title or in part; al-Zajjājī was among his students.
uncertain: His death is given as 299/912 or 320/932 (TDV).

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 78 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
